answer: Riverstone Verification Agents must deposit a unique shard of natural riverstone—collected only from designated meadow tributaries—into a public ledger. Each shard is physically traceable via mineral composition and GPS-tagged origin. The system verifies authenticity by cross-checking shard density and crystalline structure against a decentralized database updated weekly. An attacker attempting to create multiple identities must acquire or fabricate equivalent shards. Mining shale deposits near river sources yields low-quality fragments unsuitable for verification.
